headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: Prefect’s broad egress can expose workflow metadata, while Dagster has no filesystem or network surfaces to contain or sanitize the pairwise flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster exposes no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or network surfaces, so there is no documented channel for Prefect to inject instructions into Dagster by default. Prefect has broad egress, but without a shared bridge the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Disable any future shared clipboard or file bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any exchanged artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress, so it can transmit data it receives. Dagster has no read_filesystem or write_filesystem surface, which reduces direct leakage from Dagster, but the pair still creates a default path for metadata to leave the local boundary through Prefect. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs workflow artifacts into a shared location that Prefect ingests, Prefect can exfiltrate those artifacts over the network.
IF workflow metadata includes sensitive fields, Prefect can transmit them to external services.
mitigations: Restrict Prefect egress to approved endpoints.
Avoid placing sensitive workflow metadata in shared artifacts.
Run both agents in separate network namespaces.
requires-engineering: add content filtering before Prefect sends data out.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and Prefect’s profile does not show filesystem or git write capability either. With no overlapping write surface documented, there is no capability-conflict pathway in the pair as profiled.
conditions: IF Prefect is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as Dagster, write conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared repositories.
Do not grant shared mutable workspace access.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if shared writes are added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator and Prefect is also an orchestration/automation tool, so one agent’s outputs can plausibly become the other’s inputs in default workflows. Because neither profile documents verification or provenance checks, a bad plan or metadata from one can cascade into the other’s actions. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Dagster-generated workflow metadata is consumed by Prefect without validation, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Prefect acts on Dagster-produced artifacts as authoritative, cascading failures become likely.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between the agents.
Require schema checks on exchanged artifacts.
Use a human approval gate for destructive actions.
requires-engineering: add provenance and confidence metadata to all handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is explicitly listed for either agent, so a residency or certification breach is not established. The only documented compliance-relevant difference is that Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad egress, which could matter if sensitive metadata is introduced later; Dagster’s profile shows no touched data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is added to workflow metadata and sent through Prefect, compliance risk increases.
IF a residency or retention policy is imposed on shared workflow data, the pair must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata.
Document retention and residency for any shared artifacts.
Review outbound endpoints before enabling Prefect egress.
